text:
Alex: Quick sync — proposing a pragmatic convergence plan for SDK transports. idea: tiny per-language adapters + a lightweight browser bridge. thoughts?
Maya: +1 to adapters. browsers are tricky. gRPC-web vs websocket fallback?
Sam: Agree on adapters. Suggestion: native SDKs default to HTTP/2 streaming; browsers use websocket or gRPC-web only if needed.
Lina: Node/Deno can do http2/grpc. ops wants minimal protocol complexity in prod.
Alex: Tradeoffs we discussed:
- HTTP/2 streaming: low latency and multiplexing, good for long-lived streams and kv-cache reuse, but many proxies mangle it.
- gRPC: strong typing but heavier per-lang bindings and ops plumbing. gRPC-web needs envoy or proxy.
- Websocket: simplest for browsers, but lacks native HTTP headers unless we emulate them in frames.
Maya: For retries & pagination we need consistent semantics. Should transports surface resume tokens and idempotency hints?
Sam: Yes. Proposal: server emits Resume-Token header/frame for resumable responses. SDK iterators expose resume_token on page boundaries.
Lina: For streaming (chat/partial tokens) server should emit periodic checkpoint frames (every N tokens) containing a resume token so clients can snapshot state. Client opt-in to checkpoint frequency.
Alex: Checkpoints + explicit final resume token on chunk boundaries. Clients can ignore frequent checkpoints if they prefer.
Maya: Retries: only retry idempotent operations. For paginated iterators, retry should use resume token to fetch the next page rather than naive rewind. Backoff: jittered exponential.
Sam: Also define per-call deadline propagated to transport, plus SDK-level cancel. Timeouts default to reasonable values.
Lina: Ergonomics across languages: TS/Python -> async iterators; Go -> stream interface that returns chunks or uses channel. Adapters implement a minimal shape: Connect(headers) -> Stream with Send/Recv/Close.
Alex: Pseudo-shape:
```
interface TransportAdapter {
  connect(reqHeaders): Stream
}
interface Stream {
  send(payload)
  recv(): Message | EOF
  close()
}
```
Maya: Keep SDK core transport-agnostic. Build http2, grpc, websocket adapters.
Sam: RetryPolicy config: max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, retriable_codes. Defaults provided, configurable.
Lina: Bridge (for browser) should be stateless frame proxy with connection affinity to avoid breaking stream state. Could run as a lightweight sidecar or edge lambda.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: helm chart scaffolded for bridge-proxy v1 (canary) — run /deploy bridge-proxy/canary to test.
Alex: Rollout plan: 1) land TransportAdapter interface in TS/Python/Go SDKs. 2) ship http2 + websocket adapters. 3) add resume-token checkpoint frames server-side. 4) docs + examples for async iterators + retry policy. 5) optional gRPC adapter if requested.
Maya: Adapters should emit telemetry: conn_open, conn_close, reconnects, frame_latency, resume_retries with consistent metric names across langs.
Sam: We should test common corporate proxies (Cloudflare, corp proxies) behavior in staging.
Lina: I'll draft a runbook for bridge-proxy troubleshooting (sticky sessions, TLS passthrough).
Alex: Actions: @Maya draft SDK interface PR (TS + Python) this week; @Sam spike Go adapter using net/http2; @Lina spec resume-token frames and checkpoint semantics; @Alex coordinate bridge-proxy canary per devops-bot.
Maya: Example iterator usage to show resume:
```python
async for page in client.responses.paginate(req, retry_policy=default):
    process(page.items)
    if page.resume_token:
        save_token(page.resume_token)
```
Sam: Keeping transport layer minimalish helps long-term refactors.
Alex: Thanks, follow-up PRs when ready. :thumbsup:
